title: Compare and Contrast Aspects of Compliance and Regulation

sections.title: What You Are Learning
paragraphs: Cloud organizations cannot store and process data however they want.
Different data may be subject to legal requirements, contract requirements, geographic restrictions, industry standards, and retention requirements.
CompTIA wants you to recognize what requirement is controlling the data and why.

sections.title: Maestro Focus
paragraphs: Is the scenario asking who controls the data, where it may physically exist, how sensitive it is, or how long it must be preserved?
sections.callout: Ownership → who controls it. Locality and sovereignty → where it exists and which laws apply. Classification → how sensitive it is. Retention → how long it stays.

sections.title: Data Sovereignty
paragraphs: Data sovereignty means data is subject to the laws and regulations of the country or jurisdiction where that data is located.
Think: Where the data lives can determine which law rules it.
sections.callout: Geographic location determines which laws apply to data → data sovereignty.

sections.title: Data Ownership
paragraphs: Data ownership identifies who has authority and responsibility over the data.
An organization may use a cloud provider to store information while the organization still owns that data.
Think: The provider stores it; that does not automatically mean the provider owns it.
sections.callout: Who has responsibility or control over the information → data ownership.

sections.title: Data Locality
paragraphs: Data locality concerns the physical or geographic location where data is stored or processed.
An organization may require certain data to remain within a country, within a region, or within a specific geographic boundary.
Think: Where exactly is my data?
sections.callout: Data must remain in a particular place → data locality.

sections.title: Data Sovereignty vs. Data Locality
paragraphs: Data locality asks where data is located. Data sovereignty asks which jurisdiction's laws apply because of that location.
The organization can own data that is stored in a provider's facility; ownership and location are separate questions.

sections.title: Data Classification
paragraphs: Data classification places information into categories based on characteristics such as sensitivity or importance.
Different classifications may require different protections. Not every piece of data deserves the same security treatment.
sections.callout: Information must be categorized according to sensitivity → data classification.

sections.title: Data Retention
paragraphs: Data retention defines how long information must be kept.
Different requirements may force an organization to retain information even when it would otherwise prefer to delete it.

entries.title: Litigation Hold
paragraphs: A litigation hold prevents relevant data from being deleted when it may be needed for legal proceedings.
Normal deletion or retention schedules may need to be suspended. Think: A legal case says not to touch that data.
entries.recognitionCue: Data must be preserved because of current or expected litigation → litigation hold.

entries.title: Contractual Retention
paragraphs: A contract may require data to remain available for a defined period. Think: We agreed to keep it.
entries.recognitionCue: A contract dictates how long data must remain → contractual retention.

entries.title: Regulatory Retention
paragraphs: Laws or regulations may require certain records to be kept for a specified period. Think: The rule says we must keep it.
entries.recognitionCue: Government or industry regulation dictates retention → regulatory retention.

entries.title: Systems and Organization Controls 2 (SOC 2)
paragraphs: SOC 2 deals with controls used by service organizations to protect customer information and operate trustworthy services.
Think: Service organization controls and assurance.
entries.recognitionCue: A cloud or service provider needs independent assurance around organizational controls → SOC 2.

entries.title: Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard (PCI DSS)
paragraphs: PCI DSS applies to environments that store, process, or transmit payment card information.
Think: Credit or debit card data.
entries.recognitionCue: The environment handles payment card data → PCI DSS.

entries.title: International Organization for Standardization (ISO) 27001
paragraphs: ISO/IEC 27001 provides requirements for establishing and maintaining an information security management system.
Think: Formal, organization-wide information security management.
entries.recognitionCue: An internationally recognized information security management framework → ISO 27001.

entries.title: Cloud Security Alliance
paragraphs: The Cloud Security Alliance (CSA) develops cloud-focused security guidance and resources.
Think: Security guidance specifically aimed at cloud computing.
entries.recognitionCue: Cloud-specific security guidance or best practices → Cloud Security Alliance.

entries.title: Data Sovereignty vs. Data Locality
paragraphs: Locality means where. Sovereignty means law or jurisdiction.

entries.title: Ownership vs. Location
paragraphs: The organization can own data that is stored in a provider's facility. Ownership and location are separate questions.

entries.title: Litigation Hold vs. Normal Retention
paragraphs: A litigation hold can override routine deletion. If legal proceedings require preservation, do not delete the data merely because the normal retention period expired.
